Title #3. 13-4, beat PIT 20-9 in the Champs Bowl.
7-10. Took QB Jason Latham #1 overall in the 2038 draft.
Jason Latham's rookie year: Offensive Rookie of the Year.
11-6. Lost the Champs Bowl 24-27 to HOU.
17-0, a perfect regular season, then lost in the Divisional round. Latham MVP: 5,257 yds, 40 TD, 3 INT.
Title #4, Latham's ring. 11-6, beat CIN 19-15 in the Champs Bowl.
8-9 and missed the playoffs, but Latham won his 2nd MVP.
12-5, lost in the Conference round. Latham MVP #3: 5,106 yds, 39 TD, 3 INT.
14-3, lost in the Conference round. Latham MVP #4.
9-8, lost in the Divisional round. Latham MVP #5.

Latham's final season. He tore his ACL around W4 and young backup Reginald Haley carried them into the playoffs. Latham came back, threw 5 TD in the Conference game, then lost the Champs Bowl 27-45 to IND. Retired after 19 seasons, all in Washington.
10-7, lost in the Divisional round. Start of a 12-year playoff streak (2062-2073).
12-5. Lost the Champs Bowl 21-27 to MIA.

Title #5. 13-4, NFC #3 seed. WC: beat TB 34-31 on Tretola's 53-yd walk-off at 0:19. Div: won at 14-3 DET 22-21 (Dubose 177 KR yds and a TD). NFC: beat SEA 28-21 with a go-ahead drive from our own 1 (Harold's 50-yd catch on 3rd & 17, Anang's 2nd TD, Lazard's 3rd and 4th down breakups). Champs Bowl: beat 15-2 MIA 26-12, Haley MVP (23/31, 371 yds, 2 TD).

Title #6. 15-2, NFC #1 seed; the only losses were to GB and CLE. Haley MVP (4,722 yds, 36 TD, 5 INT). Robinson ~2,000 yds, 18 TD, All-Pro. Div: beat ATL 31-27 on Harmon's TD at 0:25. NFC: beat NO 26-14 (Robinson 185 yds, 2 TD). Champs Bowl: beat DEN 27-20, Haley MVP again.

9-8. Lost 4 straight in December; Week 18 pickups Peake, Gedeon and Kozer saved the season. WC: beat CHI on Haley to Robinson at 0:04. Div: won at ATL 23-20 in OT (Tretola walk-off). NFC: beat LAR 12-10. Champs Bowl: lost 34-37 to MIA (Tretola missed a 44).

Title #7. 12-5, #1 seed, 6-0 in the division. Rookie #1 pick Cameron Landry (WAS traded up). NFC: 'Fieldgoalbowl 1.0' over LAR (Tretola 5/5, Rogers knocked down the Hail Mary). Champs Bowl: beat CLE 20-16 from 6-16 down at half; Haley's 93-yd drive and Harmon's TD at 0:41.
8-9. Haley tore his ACL in W4 at 37 and retired; Todd Howard took over. Won the division on a three-way tiebreaker, then lost the WC 13-16 to TB ('Harry punted twice down 3').
9-8, N East champs again. HC Harry, QB Herbig. Fell to 5-8 (3-49 at CLE), then won out: 'I WILL SURVIVE.' WC: beat SEA (Carpenter HOTW). Div: lost at 15-2 ARI 16-36.

9-8, missed the playoffs, ending the 12-year streak. Started 4-0; Cappa lost 11 weeks to a torn tricep and Harold carried the offense (200 vs PHI, 181 and 3 TD vs NYG). Won W18 at PHI, but DET lost: 'We're out.'

5-12. HC Falkner, OC Jason Latham ('coming home'), DC Mannion. Traded Herbig for 39-year-old Daniel Douglas, who tore his hamstring. Blew 12-0 and 14-0 leads ('Washington lead-blowers'); 6 straight losses to finish.

9-8, #7 seed. HC Gustin. Took Christian Murphy #1 (trade with PHI) but started 37-year-old Tevin James, who threw for 650 yds and 5 TD vs SF, the all-time record. 5-8, then 4 straight wins. WC: won at ARI 24-10 (Dowling 13/120/2, Gipson 2 INT). Div: lost at DAL 20-23 after 4 WAS flags on the final drive.
3-14, the worst season in franchise history. HC Okereke (Option); BUF hired Latham away. Murphy's debut was a win at DAL (19/24, 250), then it fell apart.

4-13, the tank. PHI owned our 1st from the Murphy trade, so we sold: Kindred to GB, Murphy and Watson to TEN, Gladney to LAC. LAR winning its last game made GB's pick #1 overall. The Haul: #1 Reggie Patterson, #2 Heeney (trade with LAR), #3 Bunting, #5 Fields.
5-12. Patterson's rookie year: 3,864 yds, 20 TD, 12 INT. Still beat 12-3 SF at 3-11. SF can't beat us ('our son').

9-8, #6 seed. HC Walker (Air Raid). Patterson MVP (5,195 yds, 41 TD, 12 INT incl. playoffs). Beat NO 48-3 (Pat 466 yds, 5 TD). W18: Kamdar's 4th-down sack beat NYG 38-31. WC: won at MIN 17-15, Patterson's first playoff win. Div: lost at SF 14-24.

Title #8. 14-3, NFC #1 seed. Div: beat LAR 44-20. NFC: 'Fieldgoalbowl 2.0', 19-10 over TB (Snead 4/4, Sims INT, Dowling TD). Champs Bowl: beat KC 20-16. Patterson back-to-back MVP and Champs Bowl MVP (5,174 yds, 40 TD, 9 INT incl. playoffs). Berrios' 4th ring. Pocket GM's final season.
